note: Korean home cooking, restaurant dishes, street food, banchan and the Korean chains — written for a catalogue that began Malaysian and is becoming Asian. WEB SEARCH WAS UNAVAILABLE FOR THIS ROUND: every figure here is a model estimate reasoned from the dish's own ingredients and anchored against comparable rows already in the catalogue (the pan-Asian round's Korean dishes, the Chinese and Malaysian noodle rows, the MyFCD and USDA component rows). Nothing was read off a published table, so every row is verified:false and source:model_estimate — including the chain rows, whose figures Korean chains do publish and which are therefore the cheapest to verify in a later round. The Korean dishes the pan-Asian round and the Malaysian-chain rounds already landed — kimchi jjigae, sundubu jjigae, budae jjigae, dolsot bibimbap, kimchi fried rice, japchae, jjajangmyeon, jjamppong, kimbap, samgyeopsal, samgyetang, dakgalbi, haemul pajeon, injeolmi bingsu, the Korean corn dogs, the five Korean-fried-chicken rows, the Bonchon items, cheese and rose tteokbokki, bulgogi beef, Seoul Garden, Daorae, Sae Ma Eul — are deliberately absent. NO SPIRITS: soju, makgeolli and beer carry most of their calories as ethanol, which is not one of the three macros, so an honest carbs/protein/fat row cannot state them and the loader's Atwater check would refuse a fudged one. Portions are the Korean restaurant portion: a jjigae is the single-person earthenware pot it is served in, a gui portion is the grilled weight of one person's share of a shared order, and a chain chicken row is the half bird a Korean order is actually divided into.
